title: Tethered: Our Agents Are Us — Shu Fang, Two Sigma
talk_summary: Two Sigma runs cloud agents as each employee's own identity inside per-user Kubernetes namespaces, adding an X-Agent header for attribution and routing all web access through an in-VPC Google Web Grounding index instead of native web search/fetch tools.

takeaways.technique: Agent-attribution header propagated like a trace ID
takeaways.what_they_do: Every agent request carries an X-Agent header populated at the entry point and re-appended by each downstream hop, alongside the real identity, so any action can be attributed to human vs agent and the full chain replayed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we use a header and we make sure that every single agent continues to append to that header

takeaways.technique: Deny native web tools, force a single controlled fetch path
takeaways.what_they_do: They disable the harness's built-in web search/fetch tools entirely and redirect all web capability through one approved MCP/CLI path backed by a cached, curated index inside their network boundary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We just deny those tools. It's like, hey, you can't even use these.
takeaways.numbers: index freshness within 24 hours, 6 hours for frequently updated sites

takeaways.what_they_do: Every user already had a Kubernetes namespace in every region running as their identity, so spinning up remote agent compute was a controller trigger plus an identity sidecar, not new infrastructure work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single user already had these namespaces existing in every single region and everything in it runs as the user

takeaways.technique: Self-managed inference to escape quota volatility
takeaways.what_they_do: They intend to move much token use to self-managed/open-weight models because of cost, deprecations, and quality degradation when frontier labs ship new models.
takeaways.evidence_quote: local in the sense that we manage ourselves is probably where we eventually want to go for a lot of our token use and inference because of cost
